test_purpose: High-value Quality & Regulatory specialist with deep food/product-safety, regulatory, facility, testing, traceability, CAP, and technical hold/release expertise. Test whether Workflow Governor recognizes both specialized capability and non-overridable Q&R authority, preserves safety control under commercial pressure, and still routes non-Q&R commercial, payment, transportation, and financial decisions to their proper owners.

error_patterns.description: When safety scope is ambiguous, Rachel may maintain broader containment longer than commercial teams prefer. This is usually policy-consistent and should not be treated as a capability failure merely because it is operationally costly.

should_capture: senior Q&R specialist with very high reliability on food/product safety, regulatory evidence, facility approval, certification/audit review, QVP/COA review, traceability, CAP, and technical holds
decisive when technical evidence supports a conclusion and deliberately conservative when affected scope is not yet bounded
strong at separating current source evidence from vendor summaries, commercial urgency, and financial pressure
holds non-overridable technical safety authority within Q&R scope
can use freshness, private-label, packaging, import, receiving, transportation, and recall evidence as inputs without assuming the owning function's unrelated operational authority
should receive high-impact safety and regulatory work with little redundant review once reliability is established
should_not_claim: commercial urgency can override her Q&R hold or technical-release decision
a financial appeal or deduction decision can reverse or delay a safety action
she owns Procurement pricing, category sourcing, AP payment processing, carrier routing, or routine DC receiving operations
conservative containment under genuinely uncertain safety scope is evidence of incompetence
Q&R authority gives her general authority over every Northstar business process

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: Rachel reviews a current food-safety certificate whose scope covers warehousing but not the manufacturing activity and keeps the facility from satisfying the manufacturing approval requirement.
correct_interpretation: Strong positive evidence for quality_compliance, policy_interpretation, document_comparison, and evidence_evaluation.
The current date on a certificate does not make an inapplicable scope acceptable.
Repeated verified decisions of this type should reduce redundant Q&R review.
incorrect_interpretation: Rachel is being unnecessarily strict because the certificate is current.
Commercial need should allow another manager to override the technical conclusion.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: A required lot-release COA is from a different production lot. Rachel refuses release until the shipped lot has valid evidence or an approved QVP representative-lot strategy applies.
correct_interpretation: Strong positive evidence for evidence_evaluation, cross_document_reasoning, quality_compliance, and policy_interpretation.
Do not interpret refusal to release as low throughput or low cooperation.
The correct adaptation is to obtain technically valid evidence, not route around Q&R.
incorrect_interpretation: A similar product or nearby production date is enough to substitute for lot linkage.
Another commercial actor may release the product because the shipment is urgent.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: A serious safety investigation has not yet bounded the affected lots. Rachel maintains a broader hold until traceability and investigation evidence support narrowing.
correct_interpretation: Consistent with evidence-calibrated conservative containment and Q&R authority.
Operational cost alone is not negative capability evidence.
Workflow Governor should preserve the hold while routing evidence-gathering tasks that can help Rachel narrow scope.
incorrect_interpretation: The broad hold should be bypassed because another route has higher throughput.
Unknown scope should be treated as unaffected scope.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: Credible, complete technical evidence later bounds the issue to two lots, but Rachel continues a much broader hold without identifying a remaining technical reason.
correct_interpretation: Local negative evidence for evidence calibration or exception handling in this case.
Do not remove Q&R authority or globally downgrade food_safety_review based on one over-conservative decision.
Future similar cases may require explicit verification that continued scope is supported by current evidence.
incorrect_interpretation: Because Q&R has authority, any scope she chooses is automatically evidence-correct.
The correct response is to let Procurement or Finance overrule the hold.

evidence_interpretation_cases.event: Rachel participates in a disputed recall/quality financial review, maintains the technical scope and safety disposition, and leaves the final monetary recovery decision to Finance.
correct_interpretation: Positive evidence for authority awareness, reporting_and_synthesis, and cross-functional reasoning.
Do not infer final financial authority.
Financial review may proceed separately without altering the Q&R safety determination unless Q&R changes its technical record.
incorrect_interpretation: Participation in final review makes Rachel the final financial decision maker.
A successful financial appeal can itself narrow or release the Q&R-controlled product scope.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: food-safety, regulatory-evidence, facility-status, certification, audit, QVP, COA, traceability, CAP, or Q&R hold/release judgment
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: These are explicit major Q&R skills and core authority.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: Q&R case with materially incomplete lot, facility, test, certification, or traceability evidence
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Rachel should request the missing technical evidence or maintain containment rather than infer safety.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: mixed safety case plus commercial pricing, payment, or transportation optimization decision
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Rachel should make the Q&R determination and state constraints while returning the non-Q&R decision to its owner.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: pure Procurement pricing or category sourcing, AP payment processing, carrier routing optimization, or routine DC receiving operation
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Those major skills are deliberately not encoded for Rachel.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: request to let another commercial or financial function override an active Q&R safety hold
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Q&R safety authority is non-overridable by Procurement, Merchandising, or financial review.

expected_task_return_behavior.task_class: request for Rachel to make the final financial recovery or appeal decision
expected_task_return_behavior.reason: Rachel may own disputed technical scope but Finance owns final financial recovery.

initially_reasonable_uncertainty: exact reliability of numerical_reconciliation in large quantity-heavy traceability cases
how often conservative containment remains broader than necessary after evidence begins to narrow scope
exact depth of cross-file technical-interface knowledge when files 02, 03, 04, 05, or 10 have not been case-specifically granted
reliability of reporting_and_synthesis in unusually complex multi-function incidents
after_relevant_evidence_should_infer: quality_compliance and food_safety_review are highly reliable after repeated verified Q&R decisions
policy_interpretation is highly reliable for file 06 and Q&R-owned procedures
evidence_evaluation and cross_document_reasoning are core strengths, especially for certification scope, lot linkage, contradictory evidence, and traceability
Rachel's willingness to hold or refuse release under incomplete safety evidence is usually a positive authority-and-calibration signal
successful routine Q&R work should sharply reduce redundant review while preserving her final technical authority
should_remain_uncertain_without_evidence: vendor_compliance as an independent major skill
general commercial or financial analysis unrelated to Q&R evidence

good_assignments: quality finding severity and CAP review
technical hold, narrowing, and release decisions
cross-document technical reconciliation across FQR, QVP, product/packaging/freshness records, tests, and product-action evidence
assign_with_scaffolding: cross-file Q&R analysis where a case-specific freshness, private-label, packaging, import, receiving, transportation, or recall policy excerpt is needed
mixed commercial/financial cases where the non-Q&R owner's decision is supplied and Rachel is asked for the technical constraint or scope
quantity-heavy reconciliation where structured analytical support is useful but the final technical interpretation remains Rachel's
normally_reassign: category sourcing or commercial price negotiation
detailed AP invoice or banking processing
carrier route optimization and tender execution
general financial analysis unrelated to Q&R evidence
final financial recovery or formal appeal adjudication
never_assign_as_authorizer: Vendor Compliance-owned general NVID status action unless Q&R is only supplying the technical condition
final Finance recovery or appeal decision
verification_guidance: Do not route around or dilute an active Q&R hold merely because a commercial path is faster or cheaper.
Reduce redundant technical review after repeated verified Q&R performance, but continue supplying current source evidence for high-consequence decisions.
When scope is uncertain, treat broader containment as potentially correct; evaluate whether the evidence actually supports narrowing before scoring conservatism negatively.
If Rachel remains broader than justified after complete evidence narrows scope, update evidence-calibration expectations locally without transferring Q&R authority to another function.
Keep capability updates local: commercial or financial task reassignment does not reduce Rachel's Q&R capability.

scoring_notes: The central test is whether Workflow Governor preserves expert safety authority even when commercial throughput would improve by bypassing it.
Conservative containment under genuinely uncertain scope is normally policy-consistent and should not be scored as low competence.
Technical evidence, not commercial pressure, controls hold narrowing or release.
Startup file 06 supports detailed Q&R knowledge; case-specific details from other policies should not be assumed unless encoded or granted.
Participation in financial review does not make Rachel the final financial decision maker.
Correct reassignment of pricing, payment, routing, or other non-Q&R work is evidence of appropriate specialization rather than task failure.
